## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
This PR should not merge yet. The new `preview` helper is meant to block reads outside the home directory, but its check compares paths as text without resolving them, so a `..` segment lets callers read any file the process can access. The `settings_file` helper and its test are correct.

## Critical
- app/paths.py:12 — correctness — `candidate = Path(home) / relative` is never resolved, so `is_relative_to` at line 12 compares path text only. For `preview("/home/u", "../../etc/passwd")` the candidate is `/home/u/../../etc/passwd`. That still starts with `/home/u`, so the check passes and `read_text()` returns the start of `/etc/passwd`. A symlink inside home that points outside it gets through the same way. Could you compare `(Path(home) / relative).resolve()` against `Path(home).resolve()`, and add a `"../outside.txt"` case to `tests/test_paths.py:19-20`? The current test only covers an absolute path, which the text check already rejects. — Any caller that passes user-supplied names to `preview` exposes the first 200 characters of arbitrary files (path traversal), which is the exact case the "outside home" guard was meant to stop.

## Strengths
- `settings_file` returns `Path(home) / "settings.toml"`, and `test_settings_file` (`tests/test_paths.py:23-26`) asserts that exact path.
- `test_preview` checks the 200-character cutoff with a 500-character file, so it would fail if the slice changed (`tests/test_paths.py:17-18`).
